title: Prime Minister Conferred with “Oliy Darajali Do’stlik” Order, Uzbekistan’s highest honour for foreign leaders
body_text:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi was today conferred with the “Oliy Darajali Do’stlik” Order (Order of Highest Friendship) by the President of Uzbekistan, H.E. Shavkat Mirziyoyev for his contribution to the strengthening of friendship between the two countries. This is Uzbekistan’s highest honour for foreign leaders.
Accepting the honour, Prime Minister Modi dedicated the accolade to the 1.4 billion people of India and conveyed that it is a symbol of the enduring friendship between the two countries and civilisations. He noted that the words of appreciation spoken for him by President Mirziyoyev was a tribute to the age-old friendship between India and Uzbekistan and their shared heritage. Prime Minister further added that the honour brings added responsibility for India to work together with Uzbekistan as Global South partners for the betterment of humanity.
The conferment of the “Oliy Darajali Do’stlik” Order reflects the deep-rooted civilisational ties and the steadily deepening India-Uzbekistan Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
****
MJPS/SS/VJ

enrichment.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was conferred with Uzbekistan's highest honour for foreign leaders, the "Oliy Darajali Do'stlik" Order (Order of Highest Friendship), by President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, in recognition of his contribution to strengthening India-Uzbekistan friendship. Modi dedicated the honour to India's 1.4 billion citizens, calling it a symbol of enduring civilisational ties, and pledged deeper cooperation as Global South partners.
enrichment.context: India and Uzbekistan share historical and civilisational links dating back to the Silk Road era, and bilateral relations have been elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in recent years, with growing cooperation in trade, defence, connectivity, and culture. Indian leaders have received similar top state honours from several countries in recent years (such as from Russia, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Egypt, and others), reflecting India's expanding diplomatic outreach and its growing profile as a leader of the Global South. Such honours are largely symbolic gestures of goodwill and do not entail policy or legal change, though they often accompany or follow substantive bilateral agreements and state visits.
